simple.meaning: רֹמַח (rômach) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a lance (as thrown ); especially the iron point.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Numbers 25:7. The surrounding context includes family line, blood, priesthood, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רֹמַח (H7420) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: רֹמַח (rômach) / H7420 is traced through Numbers 25:7, Judges 5:8, 1 Kings 18:28, 1 Chronicles 12:9 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: When Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from the middle of the congregation, and took a spear in his hand.
They cried aloud, and cut themselves in their way with knives and lances, until the blood gushed out on them.
Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
Of the children of Simeon, mighty men of valor for the war: seven thousand one hundred.
He put shields and spears in every city, and made them exceedingly strong. Judah and Benjamin belonged to him.

For he said to Judah, “Let’s build these cities, and make walls around them, with towers, gates, and bars. The land is yet before us, because we have sought Yahweh our God. We have sought him, and he has given us rest on every side.” So they built and prospered.

Moreover Amaziah gathered Judah together, and ordered them according to their fathers’ houses, under captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, even all Judah and Benjamin. He counted them from twenty years old and upward, and found that there were three hundred thousand chosen men, able to go out to war, who could handle spear and shield.
Uzziah prepared for them, even for all the army, shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slinging.

But when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repairing of the walls of Jerusalem went forward, and that the breaches began to be filled, they were very angry;
Judah said, “The strength of the bearers of burdens is fading, and there is much rubble; so that we are not able to build the wall.”
When our enemies heard that it was known to us, and God had brought their counsel to nothing, all of us returned to the wall, everyone to his work.
Harness the horses, and get up, you horsemen,

“ ‘ “Those who dwell in the cities of Israel will go out, and will make fires of the weapons and burn them, both the shields and the bucklers, the bows and the arrows, and the war clubs and the spears, and they will make fires with them for seven years;

definitions.short: a lance (as thrown ); especially the iron point
definitions.full: H7420. romach רֹ֫מַח noun [masculine] spear, lance (etymology unknown; Aramaic רוּמְחָא , ; Arabic ; Ethiopic ); — often + קֶשֶׁת מָגֵן, צִנָּה, חֶרֶב, , etc.; — absolute ׳ר Judg 5:8 ; Num 25:7 (P), Ezek 39:9 ; 1Chr 12:9 ; 12:25 (van d. H. v. 12:8 ; v. 12:24 ), 2Chr 14:7 ; 25:5 ; plural רְמָחִים 1Kin 18:28 ; Jer 46:4 ; Joel 4:10; Neh 4:10 ; 4:15 ; 2Chr 11:12 ; 26:14 ; suffix רָמְחֵיהֶם Neh 4:7 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to hurl ;
